title: AI across cs.AI and neighboring arXiv fields — 8 highlighted papers
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred ranking, and citation evidence is limited for these very recent papers.

sections.title: ScaleVLA: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models to 552 Billion Parameters
sections.abstract: The authors connect a 552B vision-language backbone to an action diffusion transformer and report improved robot sample efficiency, generalization, and real-world charger insertion compared with smaller backbones.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce ScaleVLA, comparing VLM backbones from 2B to 552B under shared training and reporting improvements on several robot-policy measures.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors note the 552B setup requires more hardware; the real-world charger result is a small 10-trial comparison.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Contemporaneous technical summaries at ExplainX, Emergent, and AI Weekly, as well as a Hugging Face paper listing, make it one of the clearest externally surfaced papers in the batch.

sections.title: ViRA: Toward Ultra-High-Resolution Visual Agents via Cross-Input Relative Policy Optimization
sections.abstract: ViRA trains visual agents with contrast sets of near-identical high-resolution images so successful answers depend on reading changed evidence, reporting 63.3% set accuracy versus 59.3% for GRPO at maximum resolution.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose Cross-Input Relative Policy Optimization (CrossRPO), rewarding success across a contrast set rather than a plausible answer on one image.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors state the real-photo benchmark has only 78 indoor sets from one camera, the larger benchmark uses edited images, and CrossRPO was tested on one family of base models.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A contemporaneous technical analysis at BedrockNews, the public project repository, and cross-listing in vision and AI provide checkable visibility and relevance to visual-agent evaluation.

sections.title: ForceHarness: Turning Force into Action and Physics for Frozen Frontier Models
sections.abstract: ForceHarness gives frozen multimodal models calibrated physical summaries and self-terminating force-control primitives, reporting higher success on a real robot and two simulation benchmarks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors combine force calibration, self-terminating primitives, and physics translation, and introduce HiddenPhys to compare frozen models with force-aware policies and controllers.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors report that model-call delays prevent reactive coordination, the primitive menu is fixed, and ablations were run only in simulation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A robotics explainer at Physical AI News, the project page, and a public HiddenPhys dataset listing provide independent technical visibility and reproducible artifacts.

sections.title: How VLMs Plan What's Next
sections.abstract: Through causal interventions in Qwen3-VL, the authors describe binding, relay, gaze, and language components that select image regions and track progress while generating multi-object descriptions.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors identify a causal, modular mechanism for visual selection and progress tracking, tested across input formats, photographs, languages, and Qwen3-VL sizes from 2B to 32B.
sections.unique_caveat: Central causal tests use a controlled synthetic retrieval task in Qwen3-VL; the paper does not establish that the same mechanism applies to other model families.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It is cross-listed in three core AI categories and has a contemporaneous technical summary at ZeroHour alongside the authors' reproduction repository.

sections.title: Latent Lattice Language Models
sections.abstract: The paper adds recurrent per-layer latent streams that condition a language model's residual stream and reports lower validation perplexity on FineWeb-Edu than parameter-matched Transformer baselines.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce persistent horizontal latent states that directly condition attention, KV-cache writes, MLP computation, and decoding, reporting gains across Transformer and state-space variants.
sections.unique_caveat: The headline evidence is validation perplexity after training on 20B FineWeb-Edu tokens; downstream task performance is not established by the abstract results.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper spans three core categories and received a contemporaneous technical explainer at AIModeling, giving it broader independent visibility than a single-category announcement.

sections.title: FaceJev: Direct Visual Decisions for Face Forgery Detection
sections.abstract: FaceJev predicts anomalies in eight facial parts from an MLLM's answer logits, using PartForensics and FS-GRPO, and reports a 7.25-point gain over the strongest baseline on unseen manipulations.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors contribute direct part-level visual decisions, a dataset of about 160,000 images, and an optimization method that compares each part decision with its alternative.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported generalization result concerns the manipulation types and image collection evaluated; the abstract does not establish performance across all real-world forgery sources.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A contemporaneous explainer at Physical AI News and the paper's explicitly part-labeled dataset provide checkable visibility and substance in the vision batch.

sections.title: SWE-WhatIf: Simulating Real Users of Coding Agents from Recorded Session
sections.abstract: SWE-WhatIf replays coding-agent sessions with an adaptive user simulator grounded in recorded intent, and evaluates it on 89 sessions plus a 16-person study.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors model user intent, satisfaction criteria, and trigger conditions to generate replies that adapt to new agent trajectories rather than replaying fixed dialogue.
sections.unique_caveat: Evidence is based on 89 recorded sessions and a 16-person study; broader user populations and coding-agent settings are not established by these results.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper is cross-listed in language, AI, and human-computer interaction and has a contemporaneous research listing; the 89-session evaluation is directly relevant to agent assessment.

sections.title: Think2Listen: Evidence-Centric Learning For Agentic Audio Understanding With LALMS
sections.abstract: Think2Listen trains audio-language agents to seek discriminative acoustic evidence, revise hypotheses, and decide when to stop, reporting gains on two benchmarks spanning seven audio categories.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose training credit based on how observations change candidate states, teaching what to ask, how to use returned evidence, and when to stop.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract reports results on two benchmarks and seven audio categories; performance outside those settings remains unestablished.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It is cross-listed from Sound into cs.AI; its two benchmark results make it a relevant example of evidence-seeking agent training. Placement here reflects corpus relevance rather than a popularity measure.
